newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells U.S. not to create new damage to ties.
newsitem.headline: China tells U.S. not to create new damage to ties.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it had made representations with the United States for issuing a transit visa to Taiwan's vice-president and warned Washington not to create new damage to Sino-U.S. ties.
"We have made representations with the U.S. side," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.
Washington has granted Taiwan's Vice-President Lien Chan a visa to transit the United States en route to and from Nicaragua this week.
Lien would pass through Los Angeles on Tuesday on his way to Managua for the inauguration on Friday of President Arnoldo Aleman and spend one night in New York on his way back.
The U.S. State Department has pledged that Lien would not meet U.S. officials and would not attend any public events while in the United States.
"The U.S. side should strictly abide by its promises in this matter to avoid new damage to Sino-U.S. relations," Shen said.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
A private visit by Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui to the United States in June 1995 sent Sino-U.S. relations into a tailspin from which they have begun to recover only recently.
Beijing views Taiwan as a rebel province and has sought to push Taiwan into diplomatic isolation in its quest to forcibly bring the island under its rule.
Taiwan has tried to break out of diplomatic isolation with trips -- open or secret -- by its leaders to countries that recognise Beijing but not Taipei.
